name: Great Day Latte
detail: An ESSENTIAL part of my daily morning ritual. The fragrant scents and atmosphere remind me of my own kitchen.

name: Spot of Tea
detail: Brunch that runs late and a porch worth lingering on. Order the crab cake omelette and a second pot of tea.

name: Soul Kitchen Music Hall
detail: The room they built for the show you didn’t know you needed. Black-owned, blues-rooted, every act welcome.

name: Magnolia Roots Salon
detail: Tasha takes her time. You leave looking your best and feeling like a member of the family.

name: Iron + Ivy Boutique
detail: Curated by someone with taste — the kind of place where the owner remembers what you almost bought last time.

name: Bayside Bloom Florist
detail: Bring a friend, walk out with something seasonal and unexpected. Cash arrangements always honored.

name: B-Bob’s Downtown
detail: Open for decades, hosts Mobile’s drag scene, and one of the few places everyone has always been welcome.

name: Gallery 54
detail: Quiet, generous space. The openings are mixed crowds and that’s by design — leadership has always made room.

name: Cammie’s Old Dutch Ice Cream
detail: Bring whoever you’re with, no one is watching. Family flavor, family-friendly, family means whoever you say.

name: Bienville Square Restrooms
detail: Clean, accessible, and you don’t have to buy anything to use them. A real one when you’re downtown.

name: Mobile Public Library (Ben May)
detail: Ground floor by the entrance. Staff treats everyone like a regular — because everyone is, kind of.

name: Cathedral Square Park Restrooms
detail: Right next to where the food trucks line up Fridays. Stop here before you commit to the line.

name: The Pelican Pub
detail: Late hours, lit parking, and the staff actually says hello. Solid stop on a long drive home.

name: Callaghan’s Irish Social Club
detail: The Lammie burger and a quiet booth at the back. Hosts know every regular but never push.

name: Wintzell’s Oyster House
detail: Lit lot, big windows, the kind of place a long drive can end at without feeling like an imposition.
